RUST-NURBS-TEST20 -- independent original Python/openNURBS capture, 2026-11-13

Scope: tests only. No production code, shared gates, manifest or full gate changed.
No production fallback retired: non-NURBS, missing-library and unqualified-platform
Python routes remain necessary. Linux/glibc display bit qualification ONLY;
this is NOT Windows, Wine, macOS or portable-libm bit certification.

Original byte-identical files backed up locally under ignored legacy/retired-rust20/:
spike/test_native_nearest.py (349 lines, 15179 bytes)

Oracle runtime: bundled CPython 3.13.13, rhino3dm 8.35.0, Linux x86_64/glibc 2.43.
Oracle source SHA256:

Existing host artifact SHA256 (unchanged, used only as actual implementation):
 d15208979f4659b7ce818a46e7e3d6ecc14b35e0c442104162963d177b76d330

Capture: private capture.py executes original sources, intercepting queries_for
before return and compare(curve,tolerance). All original RNG consumption, skipped
invalid curves, knot/end queries and iteration order are retained. Expected nearest
values are directly nearest._search(curve,q,0.01,'nurbs'), never native answers or
closest_point_on_curve's potentially native verification search. Display expectations
are bridge._python_display_samples; uniform expectations are openNURBS PointAt at
T0+(T1-T0)*i/n, n=1,2,7,31 on every distinct curve. Host ClosestPoint fields are
captured separately with nearest._native_pack forced to None (original Python route).
Private helpers, logs, original files and full raw display answers are kept ignored.

Original nearest numeric coverage:
 - all 13 fixtures' 150 random plus ends/knots queries; 10 are NURBS
 - seed 77 queries; seed 20261107: 60 random attempts, 1847 queries, 27 rational curves
 - all analytic verification fixture queries (60 random plus ends/knots)
 - both equal-minima queries, in original order
 - all 13 PreparedCurve fixture groups (40 random plus ends/knots)
 - seed 31 random curves: 40 attempts, 1377 random-batch queries
New Rust: 5678 independent nearest expectations, each replayed through BOTH scalar
and batch C ABIs (11356 answers), all five floating fields as to_bits plus at_end.
Method/ambiguous are Python wrapper fields, NOT fields of the native ABI; all original
fixture host groups remain: 31 groups / 3096 queries, with all six wrapper fields
frozen. Non-NURBS cases are retained on host, not discarded from native replay.

Original display coverage:
 - all 12 fixtures x original five tolerances
 - seed 20261108: 500 attempts, 356 valid curves, 181 rational, 95 with corners;
   1780 tessellations at the unchanged five original tolerances
New Rust: all 1840 original parity cases, plus the original 400-point retry curve
and all 300 original performance-input curves at their display tolerances = 2141.
10371637 vertices replayed, with exact output count, status, initial capacity 256,
ERR_SIZE and retry protocol. Additional 3048 uniform PointAt sample cases.
762 distinct input curves; degrees 1..5 counts [45,87,406,111,113], 230 rational,
5 closed; repeated/full knots, shifted domains, tiny/large coordinate scales,
endpoints, ties, Newton first/second derivatives and display derivative probes.
No tolerance widened. No random corpus sampled down.

Framing (whitespace separated; all floats big-endian IEEE-754 hex u64):
 nurbs_curves.txt: id order count rational closed domain_lo domain_hi knot_count
                  knots[knot_count] homogeneous_cvs[4*count]
 nurbs_nearest.txt: id query_xyz[3] expected_t_xyz_distance[5] expected_at_end
 nurbs_sample.txt: id segment_count expected_xyz[3*(segment_count+1)]
 nurbs_display.txt: id tolerance expected_count expected_output_bitstream_FNV1a64
 nurbs_host.txt: one JSON array per original fixture group:
                [fixture_name,random_count,queries,all_six_ClosestPoint_fields]

Display digest is over big-endian bytes of EVERY parameter followed by EVERY xyz,
including signed zeros and vertex ordering; it is not a rounded/tolerance digest.
The raw expected text was 705324853 bytes. Compact per-case bitstream fingerprints
avoid checking in 705 MB and compile/include overhead, while count/status are also
asserted independently. FNV64 is an exact-bit regression fingerprint, not a
cryptographic proof; raw expected answers are preserved in the ignored backup.
Fixture byte hashes and exact row counts are hardcoded in Rust; host fixture SHA256
is hardcoded on host. Corpus changes require intentional integrity/count updates.

Host-only checks retained: actual r3 types and homogeneous packing, every original
fixture query group, analytic recognition/projection/ambiguity/all wrapper fields,
osnap real routing/cache, non-NURBS and missing-library fallbacks, PreparedCurve
batch-vs-scalar calls, mixed nonfinite errors/finite batch points. Added real edits
and owned snapshots, refusal success counters, invalid metadata and unqualified
batch-platform guard. Display retains real retry/counters, missing-library and
unqualified-runtime fallbacks; adds real edits and invalid tolerance refusal.
The original timing loops and comparisons remain unchanged: Near <=0.9 for each
of its three fixtures; display batch Rust < Python, plus original individual timing
reports. Existing active Python fallbacks are used, NOT a duplicate engine. These
are retained end-to-end host performance guards, not replaced by a portable Rust
microbenchmark or relaxed thresholds.

Mutation qualification (private copied Rust source, no production edits):
 - first sample tie '<' -> '<=': RED scalar curve 1 row 150 parameter bits;
   restore GREEN
 - actual native libm pow -> multiply: RED display case 248 output bitstream;
   restore GREEN
 - native uniform parameter arithmetic reassociation: RED sample 7 field 27;
   restore GREEN
 - actual host bridge._curve_display_points bypasses native: RED native counter
   assertion despite equal points; restored original host suite GREEN.
Private copies have no tools/vendor symlinks and are not git worktrees.

Final host source totals: 528 lines / 23676 bytes, versus original 583 lines /
25162 bytes: net Python reduction 55 lines / 1486 bytes. This includes new host
framing/edit/refusal/platform coverage and retains all original host query groups.
Final results: Rust 4/4, nearest host 62/62, display host 24/24; diff whitespace
check clean. Near timing ratios 0.295 / 0.101 / 0.073 on the last host run (original
<=0.9 limits unchanged). Native host artifact byte hash unchanged.

Validation: cargo test --manifest-path native/pure_core/Cargo.toml --release
--test nurbs_golden; both modified host suites with bundled Python and existing
release artifact. Full gate and commit deliberately NOT run (owner scope).
